claims.claim: The roadmap and the PRD make opposite promises about the same capability: the roadmap's ApplicationSet entry states that ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet children will not be implemented and that teardown remains a manual operator action performed one Application at a time, while the PRD's goal 2 ships exactly that as the Reverse deletionOrder, which deletes applications in the reverse order of the rollingSync steps and waits for each to be fully deleted before the next. Nobody owns the call: the PRD's sponsors, reviewers and approvers are all TBD, and the incident review explicitly logged the disagreement and declined to decide it.

The impersonation rollout plan assumes a per-project gate the design says cannot exist. The platform-sync decision is that impersonation goes behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide, and that nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed; the RFC's goals state the feature can be enabled or disabled only at the system level and that once set it applies to all Argo CD Applications, and the only enablement surfaces it defines are argocd-cm, an environment variable, and a controller flag, all cluster-scoped. Field evidence already reflects the mismatch: the CI diff failures come from users describing projects where they recently enabled the sync impersonation flag, meaning a system-level switch is being reasoned about, and reported on, as if it were per-project.

Reverse deletion and parallel progressive sync steps cannot both hold. The PRD states that Reverse depends on rollingSync.steps being a strictly sequential list of match groups, one deployed and deleted at a time, and that any change letting a step contain more than one match group evaluated concurrently removes the single ordering Reverse reverses. The parallel-steps proposal is precisely that change: it puts a list of matchExpressions groups under a `parallel` key (or `parallelGroups`) so independent cluster groups sync at once, leaving no single sequence to invert.

The parallel-steps enhancement has an unstated deadline that will pass silently. The maturity review's scope call freezes `strategy.rollingSync.steps` (the matchExpressions list, one match-set per step) as the v1 shape once Progressive Sync ships Stable, and requires any change to how a step is expressed to land as a new field before that point rather than as an in-place restructuring after; the review notes this is not filed against any specific open enhancement. The parallel proposal restructures the step in place, so if Stable promotion closes first, the sketched API becomes unshippable under the backward-compatibility bar and the feature has to be redesigned around a new field.

The PRD's Risks and Mitigations section asserts there are no immediate risks to consider, and field evidence contradicts the assumption it rests on. The delete/recreate report is on an ApplicationSet configuring a rollingSync step order with the reverse deletion strategy: because Reverse waits for one Application to be fully deleted before moving to the next, an Application stuck Progressing means that wait never completes and the controller restarts the wave from the top, flipping the app between Deleting and Syncing. The incident review reproduced this in staging with the reverse deletion order, and the standing mitigation is to switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce before deleting any child by hand, that is, to turn off the strategy the PRD exists to ship.

A shipped hydrator mode depends for its correctness on something the design puts out of scope and nobody owns. The hydrator RFC lists implementing a change promotion system as its sole non-goal, and push-to-stage is defined as pushing to a different branch while relying on an external system to move changes to the deployment branch. The stale-manifest auto-sync defect is observed only in push-to-stage mode, precisely because the external promoter has not yet moved the fresh manifests and auto-sync applies whatever the stage branch last held; the platform-sync call records that the stage-branch promoter is still a shell script with no owner, and that item was parked rather than assigned.

The Stable promotion gate has no data behind it. The promotion issue adopts the argoproj feature-status bar that Stable features are tested and validated with various use cases and that issues will thereafter be tracked as bugs, but the open RollingSync defect reports that there is no counter incrementing when specChanged fires without a resulting sync operation, so the only available figure, roughly 1 in 6 Helm-parameter-only rollouts, is a headcount of support pings rather than a measured rate, and the reporter states they cannot tell whether it is 1 in 6, 1 in 60, or worse on rollouts nobody complained about. Promotion would therefore be declared on incident volume, and the same missing instrumentation means a regression after Stable is equally invisible.

The progressive-sync metrics proposal and the defect that most needs measuring describe the same blind spot without referencing each other, and the proposal misses it. The metrics ticket asks for time from detection to trigger, time per step, count of Application refreshes caused by the ApplicationSet, and which Applications a sync is waiting for; the RollingSync defect names the specific missing instrument as a counter for specChanged firing without a resulting sync operation, a case where the ApplicationSet reports the rollout complete and is not waiting on anything, so none of the four proposed metrics would ever move. The defect also notes its controller logs were at warn level and emitted no progressive-sync transition logs, so the logging alternative the metrics ticket offers does not cover it either.

Two roadmap commitments are funded from one pair. The roadmap's sharding entry records that application controller capacity for the quarter is committed to the Progressive Sync Stable punch list and that the pair owning sharding is the same pair working that list, so sharding will not start until Stable promotion closes; separately, the platform-sync call moved the dev pair off the hydrator History and Rollback work to the progressive sync deletion loop, deprioritizing it to next quarter. The roadmap still carries sharding as committed scope and the rollback ticket still reads as active work, so both promises are outstanding against capacity that the same Stable punch list has already absorbed, and the rollback ticket does not say it was deprioritized.
